items.name: Dave
items.description: A man in his late thirties who has just moved into an old house with streaky windows. Practical, dryly funny, skeptical by habit, and quietly lonely in a way he would never say aloud. He notices small physical wrongnesses before he believes anything: a chair's angle, a cold seam in a hallway, dust patterns. He wants to be taken seriously by the person he loves, and he is ashamed of how much he wants it.

items.name: Mira
items.description: Dave's partner. Warm, quick, and fond of being the reasonable one; her teasing starts as affection and sharpens into a habit of scoring points. She does not see anything in the house and treats Dave's accounts as a bit he is doing for attention. She is not cruel by design, which makes the wedge worse: she keeps expecting him to laugh along.

items.name: Hattie Vale
items.description: A spirit bound to the house, once a woman who kept its rooms and died there in the 1920s; her grave stands in the cemetery Dave walks past daily. She appears as cold air, the smell of camphor and rain, and a woman whose edges blur where the light is bad. She is courteous, formal, and starved for being addressed as a person rather than a phenomenon. She wants to be believed without being exposed.

items.name: The house on Larch Row
items.description: A narrow two-story house with a long dim hall, warped floorboards, and tall windows whose old glass is streaked in cloudy bands that smear the daylight into moving shapes. Rooms feel re-angled when Dave returns to them; furniture sits a few inches from where he left it. The hall is the spine of the haunting: cold, papered in faded green, lit by one weak bulb.
invariants: Windows remain streaked
Dim hallways
Furniture shifts on its own when unobserved

items.name: The misty cemetery
items.description: The burial ground on Dave's daily walk between the house and the rest of his life. Iron fence, gravel path, leaning stones, and morning mist that keeps its own weather. Hattie's stone is in the older row; the mist thickens there and the air smells of camphor. It is the one place where the haunting feels less like intrusion and more like an invitation.
invariants: Misty
Dave passes it every day

items.name: Respect is the hinge
items.description: The haunting answers to courtesy. Addressed plainly and without mockery, the dead can be met; mocked, filmed, tested, or talked over, they become colder, louder, and less careful with the living. Mira's teasing does not merely wound Dave; it teaches the house that he is not to be trusted with what he sees.
invariants: Contempt or ridicule sharpens and coarsens the manifestations
Plain acknowledgment allows contact

items.name: How the house shows itself
items.description: Furniture moves only when no one is looking, never in a witnessed instant. Shadow figures are fleeting, seen at the edge of vision or at the end of the hall, gone when looked at directly. Touch is possible only in low light and only when Dave is alone and calm; cold arrives first, then scent, then presence.
invariants: No witnessed instant of furniture movement
Shadow figures vanish when looked at directly

items.name: The wedge between Dave and Mira
items.description: The more Dave reports, the more Mira performs disbelief, and the more she performs it, the less he tells her. Their old intimacy of shared jokes turns into a power struggle over who gets to define what is real in their own home.
invariants: Teasing escalates rather than resolves
Dave withholds more as Mira teases more

items.name: Between disbelief and desire
items.description: Dave's sensual encounter with Hattie splits him: part of him insists it was cold, draft, grief, and a lonely man's imagination; the rest of him remembers being wanted by someone who saw him clearly. He cannot confess it to Mira without confirming every joke she has made.
invariants: Dave stays torn between disbelief and desire
The encounter cannot be easily explained away for him

items.name: Narration
items.description: Third person limited, past tense, anchored in Dave's senses and misgivings; literary, restrained, with concrete physical detail carrying the dread and the erotic charge. Scenes in the house stay close and low-lit; cemetery scenes are slower and mist-softened.
invariants: Third person limited to Dave
Past tense

items.name: Dave and Mira
items.description: Long-term partners who still love each other and have stopped listening in the same register. Affectionate on the surface, thinning underneath, with Mira holding the upper hand in any argument about what is real.

items.name: Dave and Hattie
items.description: Host and guest, then witness and witnessed, then something neither of them has a word for. Courtesy on both sides; want on both sides; the imbalance of living and dead always in the room.

args.viewpoint: Third person limited, anchored in Dave
args.tone: Restrained literary dread, cold sensuality, dry tenderness; longing held in physical detail rather than confession

chapters.title: Streaked Light
points: Dave walks through the empty house on Larch Row with the keys still warm in his hand, cataloguing the streaked windows and the long dim hall.
He sets the furniture straight by eye and starts carrying boxes; Mira arrives warm and joking and immediately rearranges his arrangement.
Alone at dusk he notices a chair has turned to face the hall; he tells himself he moved it and hears a floorboard take weight behind him.

chapters.title: The Reasonable One
points: Dave starts his daily walk past the misty cemetery and notices an old leaning stone in the front row; he begins to greet the house out of politeness, half joking.
Small wrongnesses multiply: drawer handles reversed, a lamp moved to the hall's end, a shadow figure crossing the doorway that is gone when he looks.
He tells Mira; she teases him in front of friends and films the hall theatrically, and the cold in the house sharpens in answer.
A door shuts hard enough to rattle the streaked glass, and Mira laughs it off while Dave stands in the cold seam of the hallway.

chapters.title: Camphor
points: Mira leaves for a work trip; alone for three nights, Dave stops mocking himself and speaks plainly to the empty hall.
The house answers with courtesy instead of pranks: warmth at the threshold, furniture set back the way he likes it, a smell of camphor and rain.
He sees Hattie properly for the first time at the end of the hall, blurred at the edges, and she asks him not to look away.
The chapter stops on the first touch of her cold hand and Dave's decision not to flinch.

chapters.title: The Long Hall
points: In the low light of the hall, Dave and Hattie's encounter becomes sensual, tender, and strange; he is wanted by someone who has watched him closely.
Afterward the house is quiet and the cold recedes; Dave lies awake cataloguing impossible details he cannot explain away.
By morning the hall is ordinary, the chair is where it always was, and doubt arrives with the daylight.
The chapter stops with Dave on the cemetery path, mist to his knees, unable to tell longing from grief.

chapters.title: Tests
points: Dave tries to prove the encounter was draft and grief: he seals the windows, marks the furniture with tape, and waits in the hall with a lamp all night.
The house refuses to perform for a test, and his doubts thicken; only when he apologizes for the tape does the hallway warm again.
Mira returns and the teasing resumes harder, now with an edge of hurt; Dave begins lying about what he sees to keep the peace.
The chapter stops with Dave in the cemetery at dusk, mist risen and a figure waiting between the stones that is not a shadow.

chapters.title: Her Name
points: In the mist Dave finds the leaning stone and reads the name Hattie Vale; the figure at the fence waits to be recognized rather than approached.
He tells Mira the truth about the grave, and she follows him there to be kind in the wrong way, mocking the stone and calling the whole thing a bit.
The mist turns hard and cold; something in the cemetery withdraws, and Mira finally feels it and is frightened rather than amused.
The chapter stops with Mira giving him a hard choice, and Dave staying behind in the fog with the name still in his mouth.

chapters.title: Respect
points: Dave tells Mira plainly, without joking or begging to be believed, what happened and what he wants; she cannot believe him but stops laughing for the first time.
He declines to make the house a battlefield: he corrects the chair's angle himself and says Hattie's name aloud in the hallway, on purpose.
Hattie answers once and does not stay to be studied; the wanting is mutual and the limit is acknowledged on both sides.
The house settles, Mira and Dave end in an honest, unresolved conversation at the door, and the story stops in the dim hall with the streaked window full of morning.

args.brief: Chapter 1. Open on the empty house on Larch Row: Dave with keys, catalogue the streaked tall windows smearing daylight, the long dim hall with its one weak bulb, the smell of old paper. Establish his dry humor and his practical habit of fixing small things — he squares the furniture by eye. Mira arrives warm, joking, and rearranges things; the first exchange of teasing, affectionate but with her holding the upper hand. End at dusk: the chair he set square now faces the hall, and a floorboard takes weight behind him. Keep third person limited past tense, concrete physical detail, no ghosts shown clearly yet.

Chapter 2, "The Reasonable One". Dave establishes his daily walk past the misty cemetery and notices an old leaning stone in the front row of graves; meanwhile the house's small wrongnesses multiply — drawer handles reversed, a lamp moved to the end of the hall, a shadow figure crossing the doorway that is gone when he looks directly. He tells Mira. Her teasing escalates: she performs disbelief in front of friends, films the hall theatrically, mocks the whole thing as his bit. Under the mockery the house turns colder, coarser — a drawer dumped, the lamp knocked over. End with a door shutting hard enough to rattle the streaked glass, Mira laughing it off, Dave standing in the cold seam of the hallway. Keep supernatural events unexplained-instantaneous: no witnessed furniture movement.

Chapter 3, "Camphor". Mira leaves for a work trip; Dave is alone in the house for three nights. He stops half-mocking himself and speaks plainly to the empty hall — greeting it, apologizing for the tape and the film-making. The house answers with courtesy rather than pranks: warmth at the threshold, furniture set back the way he likes it, a smell of camphor and rain arriving before anything visible. On the third night he sees Hattie properly at the end of the dim hall — a woman whose edges blur where the light is bad, formal, courteous, starved for being addressed as a person. She asks him not to look away and not to film her; he puts the phone down. End the chapter on the first touch of her cold hand and Dave's decision not to flinch. Third person limited past, restrained and sensory; the erotic charge begins here but stops at touch.

Chapter 4, "The Long Hall". The sensual encounter. In the low bulb-lit hall, Hattie and Dave's intimacy unfolds: cold that reads as skin, camphor and rain, a woman who has watched him closely for weeks and wants to be wanted as herself rather than as a phenomenon. Write it sensual and intimate but restrained — sensation, breath, cold, touch, the smell of beeswax and old paper, the murmuring house — with clear mutual consent on both sides and no explicit anatomy. Afterward the hall goes quiet and the cold recedes; Dave lies awake cataloguing impossible details he cannot explain away, torn between disbelief and desire. Morning: the hall ordinary, the chair where it always was, doubt arriving with daylight. End at the cemetery on his daily walk with mist at his knees, unable to separate longing from grief. Keep it within Dave's senses; Hattie's interiority shown only through speech and action.

Chapter 5, "Tests". Dave tries to prove the encounter was draft, grief, and a lonely man's imagination: he seals the windows with tape, marks every piece of furniture with masking tape, sleeps in the hall with a lamp on for a whole night. The house refuses to perform for a test — nothing moves, nothing answers, and his doubt thickens. Only when he apologizes aloud for the tape and takes it down does the hallway warm again. Mira comes home; the teasing resumes harder, now with an edge of real hurt, and Dave starts lying about what he sees to keep the peace — a wedge deepening quietly. End with Dave in the cemetery at dusk, mist risen to the fence, and a figure waiting between the stones that is not a shadow and does not vanish when he looks at it. Keep the sensual/erotic charge in memory and longing, restrained.

Chapter 6, "Her Name". At dusk in the fog Dave finds the old leaning stone in the front row and reads the name Hattie Vale, died 1923 — confirming the house and the grave are the same haunting. The figure waits at the fence to be recognized, not approached. Dave tells Mira the truth about the grave; she comes to the cemetery to be kind in her own way, but her kindness is mockery — she calls the stone a bit, jokes about the inscription, films it. The mist turns hard and cold, the air smells of camphor at the wrong strength, and something in the cemetery withdraws and then pushes back: a wind with no weather, gravel shifting, sound cut out of the world. Mira finally feels it and is frightened rather than amused. End on Mira giving him a hard choice — her, or the house and everything he claims it holds — with Dave staying behind in the fog with the name still in his mouth, not answering. Keep the haunting's rule: contempt coarsens it; do not show a full attack, only withdrawal and one alarming manifestation seen indirectly.

Chapter 7, "Respect" — final chapter, must reach a definite stopping point. Morning after the cemetery. Dave goes home and tells Mira plainly, without joking and without begging to be believed: what happened in the hall, what Hattie is, that his earlier lies were cowardice. Mira cannot believe him, but for the first time she stops laughing, and admits she teased because it was easier than believing he was lonely in a way she could not reach; they do not resolve whether it was real. Dave declines to make the house a battlefield: he takes the phone away, corrects the chair's angle himself with his hands, and says Hattie's name aloud in the dim hallway on purpose, with respect, and says goodbye rather than summoning her to prove anything. Hattie answers once — a little warmth, camphor, a shadow at the hall's end that does not approach — and does not stay to be studied; the want is acknowledged on both sides and the limit is one both honor. End with Mira and Dave at the front door in unhurried honest talk, the last image the streaked window full of morning light, the chair squared to the table, the house settled. Do not add new mysteries; close the hooks.

items.name: Sable
items.description: IGN "Sable", blue-side jungler on Rengar. Builds pure damage — lethality, crit, armor penetration, no defensive item — so one combo either erases a squishy or leaves him dead. Twelve-year-old mouse with a chipped button, instant coffee between games, a jaw that clicks when he is calculating. Speaks in timers and short calls; treats every fight as a clock he has to beat.
invariants: Full-damage build only; Sable never buys defensive items.
Sable plays Rengar this game.

items.name: Bram
items.description: Top laner on Ornn. A man in his forties with a smoker going in the yard; discusses brisket temperatures and his lawn while last-hitting, counts minions out loud, and says "we scale" every time the team is behind. Slow, calm, immovable voice. Never tilts, never types in all chat, and quietly takes every side lane nobody else will look at.
invariants: Bram never tilts and never forfeits.
Bram's champion is Ornn.

items.name: Priya
items.description: Mid laner on Viktor, a nursing student on night shifts. Her building's power cut at 12:00 and her client dropped; she is gone exactly fifteen minutes and comes back at 27:00 apologizing in caps. Speaks in hospital metaphors — triage, vitals, code blue. Wants a surrender vote when she returns, then becomes the calmest voice on the team. Lives and dies by the gravity cage and the Death Ray.
invariants: Priya's disconnect lasts fifteen minutes of game clock.
Priya's champion is Viktor.

items.name: Bex
items.description: ADC on Sivir, playing on a laptop trackpad with a cat named Wonton walking over the keyboard. 0/7 before the comeback. Apologizes constantly in chat ("my b", "sorry sorry"), overextends for one extra minion, and still has the best hands on the team once the panic stops. Sivir's On the Hunt is blue's only speed button and the key to every winning push.
invariants: Bex is heavily behind before the comeback.
Bex plays on a trackpad with a cat wandering the desk.

items.name: Moth
items.description: Support on Lulu. Hyper-competitive teenager with a spreadsheet tracking enemy summoner-spell timers, called out to the second. Refuses to type "gg" before the nexus actually falls, keeps a lucky coin balanced on the monitor, takes one loud breath before every objective, and hates a wasted spell more than a lost fight.
invariants: Moth never forfeits and never types "gg" early.
Moth's champion is Lulu.

items.name: Summoner's Rift, night queue
items.description: Three lanes and two rivers, a Baron pit that opens at 20:00, Elder Dragon territory beyond. Blue base has two nexus turrets standing behind its inhibitors; red base mirrors it. Fog of war decides most fights: one missing ward turns a clean push into a slaughter, and the width of the lane mouth is the difference between a siege and a death trap.
invariants: Three lanes, inhibitors, and two nexus turrets per base.

items.name: Match economics and clock
items.description: Kills, assists, towers, inhibitors and neutral monsters all pay gold; bounties grow on a streak, so the losing team can harvest a fortune from one fed enemy. Baron Nashor appears at 20:00 and grants a team-wide buff plus empowered minions. A destroyed inhibitor pumps super minions down that lane until it rebuilds. The clock runs in minutes and seconds and is the spine of every decision in the story.
invariants: Timers are quoted as mm:ss and stay consistent.
Baron buff empowers minions and hands the pushing team the initiative.

items.name: Full-damage Rengar
items.description: Lethality and crit with no defensive item, so the engage window is one leap. Thrill of the Hunt reveals the nearest enemy and lets Sable leap from camouflage with bonus ferocity; a full-ferocity combo deletes a squishy in under a second. If the combo misses, or a shield or spell shield eats it, Sable dies almost instantly. Every ult is a single-use key, never a sustained fight.
invariants: Each ult creates one kill window and offers no second chance.
Sable dies when his engage is spoiled.

items.name: Red team and its late-game ceiling
items.description: Red: Renekton top, Lee Sin jungle, Talon mid, Draven ADC, Pyke support. Their win condition is picks and Baron pressure in the first half. Late they have no reliable ranged waveclear, every engage tool is single-target (kick, hook, dash), and shields or a spell shield spoil the combo. Renekton's damage falls off, Draven must catch axes to keep his, Pyke's resets need kills that stop coming, and Talon cannot leave after a dive. They cannot siege a grouped base.
invariants: Red's engage tools are single-target only.
Red has no sustained ranged waveclear for super minions.

items.name: The comeback line
items.description: Blue loses a Baron fight, gives up an inhibitor, and defends three super-minion sieges. Each Rengar ult converts into one kill and one objective, and the gap closes on bounties and picks rather than on a single miracle fight. The arc ends with a backdoored second inhibitor and a push under the nexus turrets.

items.name: Sable's seat
items.description: First person, past tense, from the jungler's chair: the reader only sees what Sable's screen, his team's comms and his map awareness allow. Timers, gold counts and respawn clocks are used as beats, and every teammate is characterized through the voice coming down the voice chat.

items.name: Bex and Moth, lane partners
items.description: Moth tracks Bex's summoner spells and calls his overextensions a half second before they happen; Bex apologizes and does it anyway. Their trust is rebuilt during the super-minion sieges, when a landed spell shield matters more than any apology.

args.viewpoint: First person limited — Sable, the blue-side jungler on Rengar
args.tone: Tense, fast, wry — the flat humor of a losing voice chat turning into something that believes
args.format: Eight chapters, each headed by the match clock

chapters.title: Ten Seconds of Gray Screen
points: Sable respawns at 26:12 into a base under Baron buff: 6–19 on kills, nine thousand gold behind, Priya's client dark since 12:00.
Bram counts minions out loud while tanking at the tier-two tower; Moth rattles off timers; Bex apologizes for his seventh death.
First ult: Draven steps past his own ward to catch an axe at the river mouth, and Sable deletes him in one leap.
The Baron push stalls, but Renekton and Lee Sin crack the mid inhibitor before the wave breaks — super minions are coming.

chapters.title: Fifteen Minutes
points: Wave one of super minions hits mid and the team discovers how little waveclear it has without Viktor.
Priya reconnects at 27:00 in caps, apologizing, and immediately asks for a surrender vote; Moth refuses to type gg.
Sable's second ult picks Pyke at the inhibitor; the wave breaks with the nexus untouched but two turrets bleeding.
Priya's cage buys the first clean disengage and the team settles on Bram's mantra: we scale.

chapters.title: Wave Two
points: Red returns with a fresh Baron buff and a second super wave; Talon's dive dies on Ornn's knockup.
Sable trades his own life for Draven and Lee Sin, and the gold gap shrinks to four thousand on bounties.
Red's flaws surface under pressure: single-target engage, no ranged waveclear while grouped, Renekton's fury spent on minions.
Red takes another Baron at 32:00 while the third super wave forms, and the base braces for the worst of it.

chapters.title: The Third Wave
points: The hardest siege: super minions and Baron buff in mid, a sideline wave climbing top.
Bex lands the spell shield that eats Pyke's hook and clears a wave without dying; Moth's calls go quiet and exact.
Sable's fourth ult kills Draven beside his own nexus turret and the wave finally dies at the turrets.
The base holds with the nexus exposed, and the team decides to step outside.

chapters.title: Out
points: Blue pushes out on three lanes, wins the river fight, and secures Baron at 35:40.
Priya's cage splits Red at the pit; Bram walks a super wave down mid alone, counting it.
With the buff, blue takes top tier two and the top inhibitor — the first one — and Red's nexus turrets come live.
Red respawns and blue backs off with seconds of Baron still ticking.

chapters.title: Their Late Game
points: Blue converts the Baron into mid tier two and two picks; Red turtles behind its nexus turrets.
Red's late-game ceiling shows: Renekton's damage gone, Draven's axes caught by nobody, Talon stranded after his dive.
A straight five-on-five siege costs blue three lives for nothing, and Sable admits the turrets cannot be cracked head-on.
Priya offers the alternative: bait Baron, and let Sable take the second inhibitor alone.

chapters.title: The Second Inhibitor
points: Moth's script: four of blue show at Baron while Sable waits in red's bottom jungle behind a control ward.
Bex's On the Hunt sells the bait; Red takes it and rotates to the pit, Renekton's recall already spent.
Sable backdoors the bottom inhibitor with eight seconds of vision and a stopwatch in his ear.
The second inhibitor falls, two lanes turn into super minions, and Red's base begins dying from the inside.

chapters.title: Nexus Turrets
points: Blue walks in behind two super waves; the first nexus turret falls and Red's last stand begins.
Deaths trade both ways as Bex's speed button carries blue under the second turret and Moth lands every shield.
Sable's final ult erases Draven at the nexus while Priya's Death Ray cuts the wave behind them.
The nexus falls, the win screen arrives, and Moth types gg at last.

args.brief: Chapter 1, "Ten Seconds of Gray Screen." Open in the exact instant Sable's gray screen ends and the respawn animation starts at 26:12, right after blue lost the Baron fight. Establish the disaster: 6–19 kills, roughly nine thousand gold down, blue's mid inhibitor turret already dead, Baron buff on red, and Priya's client dark since 12:00 (fifteen minutes). Give each teammate a voice and a quirk in the voice chat: Bram's calm brisket-and-lawn monologue plus his minion counting while he tanks; Moth's stopwatch timers and refusal to forfeit; Bex apologizing for his seventh death while his cat walks the keyboard. Sable is full-damage Rengar, no defensive item, one combo or death. End the chapter on the first snowball ult: Draven steps past his pink ward at the river mouth to catch an axe, Sable leaps, kills him, and the Baron push stalls — but Renekton and Lee Sin crack blue's mid inhibitor before the wave breaks, so super minions are coming. Keep first person limited, match-clock beats, quick and hard-bitten voice. Roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 2, "Fifteen Minutes." Start at 28:15 with the first super-minion wave walking into blue's base on mid. Show the defense in detail: Bram's Ornn holds the lane mouth while counting the super minions aloud, Moth calls every timer and refuses to vote surrender, Bex's Sivir clears the wave but overextends and needs saving. Bring out Priya's return properly — she is calm, speaks in hospital metaphors, apologizes, and her Viktor is behind (level and items) but her gravity cage and Death Ray are the only real waveclear blue has. Let one red player (Rengar's counterpart, Lee Sin or the Draven) talk trash in all chat, and let the reader feel red's late-game weakness without naming it outright: they can only start fights one target at a time. Snowball beat: Sable's second ult kills Pyke near the inhibitor, and the wave breaks with the nexus untouched but a tier-two turret and a nexus turret damaged. End on the team's decision and Bram's mantra "we scale," and a hook that the second wave is already forming. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 3, "Wave Two." Jump to about 29:45, the second super-minion push. Red still has no Baron buff (theirs expired), so they have to push with super minions and picks alone — show them trying the same single-key engage again and getting punished. Give each teammate a quirk beat: Bram counting the wave while quietly buying a defensive item and telling a brisket story that turns out to be about patience; Moth's stopwatch and the coin on his monitor, calling the enemy flashes exactly; Bex overextending again but landing a Ricochet that saves the wave; Priya triaging the fight like an ER and telling people who to let die. Snowball beat: Sable's third ult kills Draven, and he then trades his own life to take Lee Sin down too — the double kill plus shutdown gold closes the deficit to roughly four thousand. Make red's late-game ceiling explicit in Sable's analysis: Renekton's fury spent on minions, Pyke's resets dead, Talon can only go in once, Draven must catch axes to do damage. Then at 32:00 Baron spawns and red takes it while blue is still clearing — end the chapter with the third wave forming and red returning with the buff, and Moth saying the number. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 4, "The Third Wave." This is the hardest siege: it starts around 33:00 with Baron-buffed super minions on mid plus a side wave climbing top, so blue has to split. Show real attrition — Bram's Ornn takes the brunt and his calm finally cracks for one line before he gets it back; Moth calls every cooldown and this time his calls are perfect and quiet; Bex lands the spell shield that eats Pyke's hook and clears a wave without dying, and Moth actually says something kind; Priya works the fight like an ER, naming who she can save. Let a red player taunt in all chat and let red's comp pay for its late-game weakness: Renekton's damage is gone, Talon goes in once and is stranded, Pyke resets never come, Lee Sin's kick is single-target, nobody can clear Baron-empowered super minions. Snowball beat: Sable's fourth ult kills Draven beside the enemy's own push, and blue kills the wave at the nexus turrets. The nexus turrets survive with almost no health, and the chapter ends with the team deciding to step outside rather than wait for a fourth wave. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 5, "Out." Start around 34:20 with blue pushing out of its own base for the first time in ages — three lanes, ward line, Moth's countdown. Blue wins the river fight at 34:50 with Priya's cage splitting red and Bram's Ornn engage, and secures Baron at 35:40. Show the swing in the gold graph and the bounty math. Give each teammate a beat: Bram walks a super wave down mid alone and counts it out loud; Bex's On the Hunt is the first time her speed button matters; Moth calls the Baron pit like a surgeon; Priya directs traffic in hospital language and keeps her own Death Ray for the wave, not the champions. Snowball beat: Sable's fifth ult kills Talon before the Baron fight and his sixth ult kills Lee Sin at the pit. Then with the Baron buff blue takes top tier two and the top inhibitor — the FIRST inhibitor of the game for blue — and red's nexus turrets go live. End with red respawning, blue backing off with the buff still ticking, and the knowledge that now they have to do it again. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 6, "Their Late Game." Around 37:20 to 40:00. Blue converts the remaining Baron window into mid tier two and two more picks, and red turtles behind its nexus turrets. Make red's late-game ceiling explicit and specific through Sable's analysis and the fight itself: Renekton's damage has evaporated, Draven must catch axes so he cannot kite backwards, Pyke's resets need kills red no longer gets, Talon can only enter once and cannot leave, Lee Sin's kick is a single-target tool against a team standing together — and none of them can clear a wave, so the super minions blue creates are permanent pressure. Then the failure: a straight five-on-five siege under red's nexus turrets costs blue three lives for nothing, and Sable admits the turrets cannot be cracked head-on while red is home. End with Priya proposing the alternative — bait Baron, and let Sable take the second inhibitor alone — and the team arguing about it before agreeing, with Moth's stopwatch and Bram's implicit trust. Bring out each teammate's quirk one more time before the plan: Bex apologizing and then committing, Moth refusing to vote gg, Bram counting. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 7, "The Second Inhibitor." Start around 40:20 with the plan going live: four of blue show at the Baron pit at 41:20 while Sable waits in red's bottom-side jungle behind a control ward, with his ult at zero and his heart in his throat. Show the tension in the bait: Bex's On the Hunt carrying the four of blue into red's vision, Moth counting red's rotations to the second, Priya holding her cage for the exit instead of the entrance, Bram walking a super wave mid so red's base keeps bleeding. Renekton's recall is already spent, red takes the bait and rotates to the pit. Sable's backdoor against the second inhibitor — actually the mid inhibitor is the second one blue destroys; make it clear this is the second inhibitor of the game for blue. Show the turret hurting him, ferocity management, one ult used for the escape when Pyke comes back, the eight seconds of vision, and Moth's voice in his ear counting the enemy respawns.
